source.title: Symmetries, flat minima, and the conserved quantities of gradient flow
source.authors: Bo Zhao; I. Ganev; R. Walters; Rose Yu; Nima Dehmamy

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper, including appendices; no relevant truncation is apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper varies conserved-quantity values and measures convergence and Hessian eigenvalue distributions in trained networks, relating these properties to sharpness and possible generalizability. It does not measure the training–test generalization gap itself.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 ensemble accuracy and adversarial-attack results test a transformation for robustness, not the claim versions about natural-label generalization, width, architecture comparisons, optimizers, batch size, dropout, sharpness-gap rankings, or memorized-example removal. Mentioned literature on flat minima and generalization is cited prior work. Training curves measure convergence, not the cataloged generalization behavior.
record.test_reason: The study measures convergence, Hessian eigenvalues, and transformed-ensemble performance. It does not test any listed version. In particular, Appendix H measures unnormalized Hessian sharpness without training–test gaps, magnitude-scaled perturbations, or comparisons of generalization measures. The sharpness–generalization connection motivates the work but remains untested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the generalization-related conclusion: conserved quantities relate to convergence and Hessian sharpness, while a systematic study of their relationship to generalization remains future work. The broader paper also concludes that its symmetry framework enables ensemble construction with robustness improvements under certain attacks.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies symmetries and conserved quantities, with experiments on convergence, Hessian eigenvalues, and symmetry-based ensembles; it does not reproduce the methods or measures in the listed claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization and conserved-quantity values are varied in convergence and Hessian experiments; transformation magnitude and attack type affect ensemble results.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendices H.1–H.2 relate conserved quantities to Hessian curvature. In the higher-dimensional linear experiment, 700 of 750 eigenvalues have magnitude at most 0.001; the center of the remaining eigenvalue distribution correlates positively with Q. Nonlinear relationships are more complicated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conserved-quantity values are related to unnormalized Hessian sharpness in the tested two-layer networks; their relationship to generalization gaps is not measured.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix I reports that symmetry-based CIFAR-10 ensembles approximately preserve accuracy for small transformations and improve robustness under FGSM attacks, while providing negligible robustness improvement under PGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-dependent symmetry transformations can produce ensembles that preserve clean accuracy for small transformations and improve robustness under some attacks.

record.problems: The generalization discussion does not report a direct generalization measurement; the authors characterize the larger-network sharpness relationship as possibly relevant to generalizability and identify systematic study of conserved quantities versus generalization as future work. Hessian experiments report distributions and correlations, not test-error gaps.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying result rows. The appendix H.2 Hessian measurements concern sharpness, not the gap named in V7; appendix I concerns transformed-model accuracy and robustness, not the claim versions.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization regimes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps, and its ranking relative to norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Correct the record's tests/T2 classification to discusses/T6. No qualifying rows or verdicts are warranted. The relevant nonqualifying experiments are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of train–test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
